correctness.rationale: For rotation-invariant probability measures on B_d with E R²=s∈(0,1], d≥2, the affine Gram matrix is diag(1,s/d,...), giving exact evaluation kernel 1+(d/s)x·y and sharp norm E Psi_d((d/s)R), reached on ∂B_d by sign-valued data. The density of Theta1 gives Psi_d prime and double prime; H(a)=aPsi_d'(a)-2(Psi_d(a)-1) has derivative sign(d-a²), positive on (1,sqrt(d)) and ultimately negative, so unique a_d>sqrt(d). For g(t)=Psi_d((d/s)sqrt(t)), g switches strictly convex to concave, and the smallest concave majorant is the chord from (0,1) to tau=min(1,(s a_d/d)²) followed by g; Jensen yields exact bound and strict contact/equality uniqueness. Planar Psi_2 gives a_2=2.5365589892306 and transitions 4/a_2², 2/a_2; d=3 a_3=3 and every optimal law is R²=s. Independent numeric root/integration and finitely discretized two-radius searches corroborated d=2..5 with several s, not the continuum proof.
